Skip to main contentBanbury pub praised for the quality and standards of its toilets at Loo of the Year Awards
The annual awards aim to shine a spotlight on the best maintained public and commercial toilets in the UK.
A Banbury pub has received praise for the quality and standards of its customer toilets at the Loo of the Year Awards 2026.
The Exchange, a JD Wetherspoon pub on Banbury High Street, has been awarded a platinum plus grading by inspectors as part of this year's awards.
Manager of The Exchange, Paul Rutherford, said: “We are delighted with the grading. Staff at the pub ensure the toilets are in excellent condition at all times and it is great that this has been recognised by the inspectors.”
The recognition follows an unannounced inspection by Loo of the Year Awards inspectors, who found the pub's facilities met the criteria for the competition's second-highest grading.
Toilets are assessed against criteria, including décor and maintenance, cleanliness, accessibility, handwashing and drying equipment, and overall management.
Facilities are graded bronze, silver, gold, platinum, platinum plus or diamond, with those deemed unacceptable receiving no grading.
Toilets awarded a diamond grading are then considered for the national and overall Loo of the Year Awards.
Managing director of the Loo of the Year Awards 2026, Becky Wall, said: “The toilets at The Exchange have been independently assessed against the Loo of the Year Awards’ 101 criteria, recognising the standard of the facilities, their cleanliness, maintenance and overall presentation.
The Loo of the Year Awards have been held annually since 1987, with inspectors typically visiting around 1,500 facilities each year.
“The pub thoroughly deserves its platinum plus grading.”

XRP (CRYPTO: XRP) has now fallen more than 70% from its all-time high since 2013. After the first two declines, the coin kept falling and took years to recover. The most recent decline began at the $3.65 peak on July 17, 2025, and much of that gain has been lost since Wall Street introduced spot ETFs.
Currently, XRP trades around 97 cents, which is 73.5% below that peak, and it has fallen 47% in 2026, following a 26.9% drop over the past 30 days. So what happened to XRP after each earlier fall from its all-time high, and how long did holders wait to recover?
XRP Has Dropped 70% From Its Peak Three Times Since 2013
The following table summarizes weekly closes, so each peak noted is below the intraday high. For instance, XRP’s best weekly close in 2025 was $3.46, compared with the intraday all-time high of $3.65.

In both earlier episodes, the first close below the 70% threshold proved to be a temporary stop, and XRP kept falling. The 2014 drop fell to 92% below its peak, while the 2018 decline fell to 95% below. A year after each drop, XRP remained below the 70% crossing price, trading at $0.0089 in 2015 compared to $0.010, and 31 cents in 2019 compared to 91 cents.
The 2018 episode is particularly relevant for current holders because XRP was a well-known and widely traded coin by then. Sellers maintained control for years, pushing XRP down to 15 cents during the March 2020 pandemic sell-off, and it lingered at 24 cents two years after hitting 70%.
XRP Needs a 277% Gain to Reach Its $3.65 All-Time High Again
From its current price of approximately 97 cents, XRP needs to rise by 277% to return to its all-time high of $3.65. The latest decline took XRP to its lowest daily close during this slide: 91 cents on November 14, about 6% below the current price. Our previous analysis explains why XRP dipped below $1 and how that critical support was broken.
Sellers have cut short every rally. For example, XRP climbed from a weekly low of 99 cents to a high of $1.70 in the week of August 23, only to decline over the following three months. Right now, XRP trades below its 50-day average of $1.27 and its 200-day average of $1.25, which are about 31% and 29% above the current price, respectively. This shows sellers are still firmly in control.
Spot ETFs and Escrow Supply Make This Drop Different
This situation differs from 2014 and 2018 for two main reasons. First, Wall Street has increased accessibility. U.S. spot XRP funds, including the Bitwise XRP ETF (NYSEARCA: XRP), had $1.08 billion in net assets on November 18, down from $1.57 billion on October 21, according to SoSoValue data. Bitwise’s SEC filings show the fund holds XRP directly.
Most of the decrease in ETF net assets is due to falling prices, as cumulative net inflows were still around $1.78 billion on November 18, close to the $1.81 billion peak on October 29. However, outflows like the $10.4 million that left on November 9 show that some investors are exiting.
The second reason is supply, as escrow releases add roughly 300 million XRP monthly, valued at about $290 million at the current price, and XRP currently has a market value of $61.4 billion. So any recovery might require far more new investment than the 2017 climb from just fractions of a cent.
How Long Could XRP Take to Reclaim Its All-Time High?
The earlier drops suggest holders could face a long wait. XRP took about three years after the 2014 fall and nearly seven years after the 2018 decline to rise above its previous peak, with the latter wait occurring during the SEC’s lawsuit against Ripple. Since this latest drop is only about three months old, history suggests XRP could still be in the early stages of a lengthy recovery, as our three-year forecast outlines.
However, if ETF inflows start to rise again while new escrow coins keep entering the market, XRP may find a bottom sooner than it did in 2014 or 2020. Our projections for XRP in 2028 illustrate the potential rebound size. Conversely, if outflows continue through 2027, the seven-year wait after the 2018 drop might be a more accurate guide.
Sam Daodu is a crypto analyst and the editor of 24/7 Wall St.'s Crypto Desk, where he covers Bitcoin, XRP, Ethereum, Solana and the altcoins investors search for most. His work focuses on price levels, spot ETF flows, on-chain data and the regulatory decisions that move crypto markets, written so a first-time buyer and a seasoned trader can both use it.
Sam has written about crypto professionally since 2019 and has published more than 2,000 articles. His analysis is syndicated on Yahoo Finance, MSN and AOL and has been cited by other crypto news sites.
